      ],
      "impact": "If the bus pins carry different signals, the GPIO driving one pin contends with the other, which can corrupt PWM output to the servo or damage the GPIO drivers. The bus pins are also loaded in a way the firmware does not expect.",

The PWM paths (R16, R18, 1 kΩ) are also permanently connected to these same servo signal nets.",
      "expected": "The spec says the two servo modes are mutually exclusive, selected by populating different jumpers.       "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R22\") (value \"0\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R10\") (value \"0\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"35\") (name \"Net-(J6-Pin_3)\")"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "Serial mode (populate R13/R14 ...): J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 are tied together into one shared bus node"}
      ],
      "impact": "The two mutually exclusive interface modes can be electrically active at once. The MAX3485 A line, the two PWM GPIOs and the servo signal pins can then contend, so the servos may receive corrupted commands or the GPIO and transceiver outputs may fight each other.",
      "confidence": 0.2
